[DSC's GIS librarian left in August 2024 and the position was never refilled. GIS requests continued.]{.lede}

Geography was DSC's single largest departmental workshop audience from 2020 to April 2024: 64 of the
{{< var instruction.total_attendees >}} UCLA-affiliated workshop attendance records from 2020 to April 2024,
more than any other department over that period as a whole.

Until they left for a faculty position in August 2024, DSC's GIS librarian handled
{{< var gis.consult_low >}} to {{< var gis.consult_high >}} booked consultations a
year (2021 to 2023) across Urban Planning, Public Affairs, Environment and
Sustainability, and Digital Humanities. They also co-taught a graduate Public Health
course, ran systemwide UC GIS workshops that reached {{< var gis.ucgis_2023 >}}
participants in 2023 alone, and managed key research datasets, including the LARIAC
aerial imagery. That demand hasn't gone
away. DSC still fields GIS requests, just without the specialist capacity to meet
them.

For context, 81 of 187 Carnegie R1 institutions ({{< var gis.r1_pct_with_gis >}})
maintain a dedicated GIS librarian, rising to {{< var gis.top25_pct_with_gis >}}
among the top 25 R&D-spending universities.

The campus mapping platform is a separate gap, a matter of ownership rather than consultation demand. UCLA's ArcGIS Online platform, used across Geography, Luskin, Fielding,
Digital Humanities, Political Science, and Social Data Science, has over 7,100
accounts and more than 3,000 active users in the past year, per an OARC governance
report from December 2025. As of that report, with no designated administrator, it was
running at over 200% of its licensed storage.
